title: Engineers build a robot hand that walks like Thing
summary:
Halloween is almost here, and engineers have built a robot hand that can walk on its own. It is inspired by Thing, the creeping hand from The Addams Family. The robot hand can balance on its fingertips and creep around. It can tap keyboard keys, push small objects and even play a simple computer game while balancing on its other fingers. If it falls, it can get back up from a flat position.

Other engineers have built walking robot hands before. But they had to make every finger the same length so the hand could balance. Human hands have fingers of different lengths and a thumb that faces the other fingers. That helps people use tools, but it makes walking harder.

A team at the Soft Robotics Lab at ETH Zurich in Switzerland tried to solve this problem. They describe the work in a preprint, which is a paper that has not been reviewed by other scientists or accepted by a journal. The team started with a robot hand with five fingers and 20 joints that move. They added a battery, motion sensors and a tiny computer. The whole thing weighs 1.8 pounds.

The team taught the hand to balance in a computer simulation. They used reinforcement learning, which rewarded the hand each time it balanced correctly. In real tests, the hand crossed 14 different places, including carpet, gravel, grass and metal. In typing tests, it hit the right key 29 out of 32 times. It also played the puzzle game Sokoban by pressing the correct arrow keys. The team says robots working in tight spaces might one day use a hand like this to reach things.
why_it_matters: Robots may one day work in tight places built for people. A hand that can move on its own might help them reach things, and the design could help robots handle objects made for human hands.
